title: Apple Event Live Blog: Here Comes the Folding iPhone
gist: Previewing Apple's September 2026 event, Wired expects a $2,000+ folding 'iPhone Ultra' and a Pro model to launch immediately, while the cheaper iPhone 18 line slips to early next year amid rising manufacturing costs and an industry-wide memory chip crisis, with Siri AI and on-device chip capability framed as the event's central narrative.

insights.claim: Wired expects Apple to debut its first folding iPhone at this event, rumored to be named the 'iPhone Ultra,' with a likely price above $2,000.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: If confirmed, this would be Apple's highest-priced iPhone tier to date, testing consumer willingness to pay a premium for foldable form factor and expanding Apple's price ladder upward.
insights.quote: The word around Silicon Valley is that it’s expected to be named the iPhone Ultra and that it will likely cost more than $2,000.

insights.claim: A Pro-tier iPhone is also expected to be announced at the same event, with both the folding iPhone and the Pro models going on sale later in September 2026.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: A fast announcement-to-sale window signals Apple's typical premium-tier launch cadence continuing unchanged even as it introduces a new foldable category.

insights.claim: The base iPhone 18 (along with the 18e and Air variants) might not arrive until early next year rather than launching alongside the premium models today, which Wired attributes partly to rising manufacturing costs and 'the ongoing memory crisis affecting the whole PC industry.'
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Ties a specific Apple product-timing decision to a broader component-market shock (memory/DRAM pricing), a signal worth cross-checking against memory-chip supplier commentary (e.g., Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) for corroborating evidence of an industry-wide memory shortage.
insights.quote: The longer wait could be because of a number of factors, including rising manufacturing costs and the ongoing memory crisis affecting the whole PC industry.

insights.claim: Wired suggests delaying the cheaper iPhone models gives Apple 'an opportunity to promote its premium handsets more heavily,' implying a deliberate mix-shift strategy toward higher-margin devices amid rising component costs.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: A margin-protection/product-mix strategy thesis relevant to modeling Apple's iPhone segment revenue and gross margin for the launch quarter if the premium-first sequencing is confirmed.
insights.quote: delaying the next generation of cheaper iPhones—the 18, the 18e, and the Air—would give Apple an opportunity to promote its premium handsets more heavily

insights.claim: New Apple Watch and Watch Ultra models are also expected to debut at today's event alongside the phones.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Confirms Apple is bundling its wearables refresh into the same September event as the flagship phone launch, consistent with its usual annual cadence.

themes.theme: Siri AI and on-device chip strategy

insights.claim: Both the new iPhones and Apple Watches will get added capabilities enabled by 'Siri AI,' the newest version of Apple's AI assistant, with expected emphasis on beefed-up chips, on-device AI, secure computing, and battery optimization messaging.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Signals Apple's core 2026 hardware narrative is on-device AI silicon differentiation rather than cloud-AI features, relevant to assessing Apple's chip roadmap and its AI positioning versus Google and OpenAI-backed rivals.

insights.claim: Wired's own testing of the Siri AI beta found it 'actually powerful and impressive,' but cautions 'there are limits to how helpful it can really be in your day-to-day life,' echoing recurring criticism of prior Siri versions.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: A tempered, from-the-source assessment that Apple's AI catch-up narrative may again underdeliver in daily use, a useful check against overly bullish market reactions to the AI messaging at the event.
insights.quote: Siri AI is actually powerful and impressive in our testing of the beta version, but just like the various Siris that came before it, there are limits to how helpful it can really be in your day-to-day life.

insights.claim: Wired does not expect Apple's rumored smart-home products — including new HomePod speakers and a Siri Visual-Intelligence camera-based smart-home device — to appear at this event, suggesting they will be saved for a separate, later launch.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Indicates Apple may be staggering its 2026 product roadmap across multiple events rather than one September mega-launch, spreading news flow (and potential stock catalysts) across the year.
insights.locator: Also notable is the list of things we're not expecting

insights.claim: Rumored AirPods with tiny built-in cameras — designed to work with voice commands to give Siri AI visual context about what the user is looking at — might debut today or could instead appear at a separate event in late September or October.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: A potential new AI-hardware form factor (camera-equipped earbuds) to watch for as a follow-on catalyst if it does not appear at this specific event.
